content: Methyl yellow, also known as 4-Dimethylaminoazobenzene or Butter Yellow, is a chemical compound with the designation C.I. 11020. It is commonly utilized as a pH indicator. In aqueous solutions with a low pH, methyl yellow exhibits a red coloration. When the pH of the solution is between 2.9 and 4.0, the compound undergoes a distinct color transition, ultimately appearing yellow at pH levels above 4.0. Historically, methyl yellow was referred to as butter yellow and was employed as a food additive. However, its use in this capacity was discontinued after its toxic properties were identified, as noted by Opie EL.
